title: Policy Sculptor: Interactive region & tier routing what‑if preview
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build an interactive 'Policy Sculptor' pane inside Console that lets customers author and validate routing policies for region selection, tier routing and fallback model variants, then run constrained what-if previews. Objectives: 1) Allow non-engineering users to compose multi-condition rules (region latency, cost target, customer tier) in an approachable editor; 2) Provide a fast preview runner that simulates a configurable traffic mix and produces per-route latency/cost/availability forecasts and a visualized fallback chain for each request path; 3) Surface safety guardrails and explainable validation errors before policy save; 4) Expose expected unit-cost and an estimated tail-latency delta when choosing model variants or enabling quantization/batching recommendations. Out of scope for this ticket: autoscaling controls, full traffic replay, and RBAC integration. Success looks like: customers can author a routing policy, run a what-if with 3 preset traffic mixes, and get clear pass/fail guidance plus a fallback visualization within 20s for small simulations.
acceptance_criteria: Editor: Users can add/remove rules combining region, latency thresholds, model variant preferences, and customer tier, persisted as a JSON policy draft

What-if runner: Runs a simulated preview for a selected policy against three saved traffic profiles (prod-like, latency-sensitive, cost-optimized) and returns a summary within 20s for 500-sample simulations
Fallback visualization: For each sample request in the preview, the UI shows the selected primary model and the exact fallback chain (variant names, regions, and reasons for fallback)
Validation: UX displays human-readable safety/lint warnings and blocking errors with actionable fixes (e.g., missing region whitelist, ambiguous tier mapping)
Cost/Latency estimates: Preview includes per-route token-cost estimate and 95th percentile latency delta compared to baseline model, calculated using runtime profiling constants from ENG-88123
Save flow: Policies that pass blocking validations can be saved to user namespace with a draft tag and a generated changelog entry
notes: Decision: Keep the policy JSON schema compact (region/tier/variant/weight/conditions) to simplify mapping to runtime routing engine; engineers prefer schema versioning over large ad-hoc DSL
Trade-off: Detailed traffic replay is valuable but costly; we surface simulated previews with synthetic sampling using histograms derived from customer telemetry instead of full replay
Accessibility: Design must support keyboard-first rule authoring (DES-1402) and colorblind-friendly heatmaps
Audit: Saved policy drafts should generate a changelog entry for console history; full audit logs handled by Private deployment workstream
